messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] P99 decode latency breach on model-gamma-prod detected 2026-03-14 03:02:34 UTC. Metrics: p95=780ms (SLO 150ms), p99=2300ms (SLO 300ms). Streaming stalls count +12% in last 5m. Routing fallback triggered for 2 regions. https://dash.internal/redwood/models/model-gamma/prod

alex: saw the alert. I'm pulling last deploys + kernel changes. @samir can you join?

samir: on it. checking last artifacts: image redwood/runtime:trt-8.6.1-build-20260313 pushed 03:00 UTC. There was a compile job that enabled new FLASH_ATTENTION kernels and a new nvcc flag in that build.

maria: saw increased tail in staging yesterday but it was noisy, didn't trigger SLO. comparing traces now.

alex: stack traces show stalls in decode loop inside attention kernel. p99 spikes align with larger context windows (~2048 tokens) and streaming clients.

june: posting flamegraphs for 03:00-03:05 window:
```
# flamegraph snippet
attention_forward: 44%\nkv_cache_lookup: 10%\ntrt_kernel_launch: 38%\nother: 8%
```
Looks like kernel launch + syncs dominate.

samir: reproducing locally with model-gamma + sequence 2k. When FLASH_ATTENTION enabled, single-step decode has variance and occasional 1.5-2s stalls. With FLASH_ATTENTION disabled, p99 drops to ~240ms.

alex: OK immediate mitigation options: 1) revert to runtime image prior to 03:00 2) set env var to disable flash kernels on prod nodes 3) route streaming traffic to compatible quantized variant (model-gamma-q4) 4) throttle some heavy streaming customers. Which do we want now?

oncall-eng: taking primary. I'll start routing 20% streaming traffic to model-gamma-q4 canary and set server-side env REDWOOD_DISABLE_FLASHATTN=1 on a small pool for testing.

devops-bot: triggered playbook step: increased dedicated pool (gamma-fallback) by 3 nodes. terraform plan/apply in progress.

samir: quick patch to disable flash at runtime (non-destructive):
```
export REDWOOD_DISABLE_FLASHATTN=1
kubectl set env deployment/gamma-runtime REDWOOD_DISABLE_FLASHATTN=1 -n prod
```
Applying to 10% of pods first.

alex: while that rolls, put a temporary route rule: if request.streaming==true and latency predicted>500ms route to gamma-q4 variant. Adding rule via routing API now.

emma-cs: customer-impact update: flagged 3 premium customers reporting interruptions to streaming sessions. CS notified and we sent short status. Need ETA for full restore.

june: after disabling flash on the canary, p95=160ms, p99=280ms on that pool. Good sign. Rolling to remaining nodes in waves of 20%.

samir: root cause hypothesis: latest TRT build enabled a new fused attention kernel with a compile-time nvcc switch `-DFAST_FLASH_ATTENTION=1` plus changes to blocksize heuristics. Under certain sequence lengths and input padding patterns we hit a pathological kernel path causing synchronous long GPU memcpy or excessive kernel retries.

alex: next steps: keep mitigation (disable flash) until we have a safe recompile. We'll pin runtime image to previous stable `redwood/runtime:trt-8.6.0-stable`. Samir, can you prepare a compiler patch to revert the heuristics and run CI perf tests?

samir: yes. I'll open PR to set blocksize fallback and remove the FAST flag. Running CI matrix across seq lens 512/1024/2048 with streaming harness. ETA for build and canary by 02:30 UTC.

oncall-eng: handing off to night oncall @june in 20m. We will keep the disable flag and pinned image. If any customer impact increases, page me.

june: ack. I'll monitor dashboards and the streaming error logs. Also scheduling a postmortem stub.

alex: note for postmortem: include decision timeline, compile flags, trace examples, affected customer list, and regression test we missed. Suggest adding streaming end-to-end test with synthetic long-prefix sessions to CI.

emma-cs: FYI sent ETA to affected customers: "Mitigation in progress; partial restoration observed; full fix ETA ~3 hours pending rebuild and validation."

devops-bot: terraform apply complete, gamma-fallback pool scaled +3 nodes.

june: current status 03:25 UTC: p95=170ms, p99=320ms, streaming stalls trending down. Keeping incident active until samir confirms safe image.

samir: PR filed: revert-fast-flag #487, running perf CI now. Also adding a runtime env `REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=baseline` to allow quick toggles.

alex: nice. After build+validation we'll do a controlled rollout and remove REDWOOD_DISABLE_FLASHATTN. Keep oncall handoff notes in the incident channel.

incident-bot: Incident status update: mitigation in place (disable flash kernels + route to q4), customers notified, p99 reduced from 2300ms -> 320ms. Incident severity: Sev2 -> monitoring.

june: closing loop: leave incident note + assign postmortem to samir/alex. I'll update the status page and link the follow-up doc.

emma-cs: will follow up proactively with the three premium customers tomorrow morning with more details and timeline.

samir: will post PR link + benchmarking artifacts when CI completes. Expect full resolution and safe re-enable later today.

alex: thanks everyone. Good coordination.
